subject: Reserved-capacity runway, GPU mix and stress acceptance questionnaire
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <procurement@stratoshealth.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@stratoshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: dedicated reservation sizing workbook + stress acceptance criteria

Jordan —

Thanks for taking the time on the intro call yesterday. Procurement and our platform engineering team consolidated the questions and attached a short workbook we use to evaluate reserved-capacity vendors. Primary asks:

- Provide sizing scenarios (A100/H100/L4 mixes) with throughput / tail-latency tradeoffs for both steady-state and peak-burst patterns.
- Define acceptance criteria for stress tests (99.9th tail, cold-cache starts, KV cache behavior).
- Confirm failover/fallback behavior when reserved pool is exhausted and whether we can pin model versions for compliance.

Can you return the completed workbook and a short narrative on the proposed reserve-runway approach by end of next week (Mar 17)? We also need a preliminary pricing band tied to the three scenarios.

Attachment: Stratos_RFP_Workbook.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Procurement
StratosHealth

From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <procurement@stratoshealth.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@stratoshealth.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: dedicated reservation sizing workbook + stress acceptance criteria

Elena —

Got it, thanks for the clear workbook. We can do the deliverable by Mar 17. A few quick clarifications so we size scenarios appropriately:

1) Steady-state profile: can you confirm average request size (tokens in / tokens out) and expected QPS per endpoint? If you have 95th/99th length percentiles, that helps.
2) Burst pattern: is burst defined as 2x, 5x, or 10x baseline for a 10–30 minute window?
3) Model mix: will you want a single large generalist model (e.g., ~70B) or poly-model routing (embedding + small chat model + large LLM for planning)?

Ben, Soojin — looping you both in for input on the acceptance criteria and fallback lanes.

-Jordan
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Mar 2028 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: RFP: dedicated reservation sizing workbook + stress acceptance criteria

Team —

Draft guidance from sales/quoting perspective below. I'll prepare pricing bands after Jordan confirms token assumptions.

Key assumptions to call out in the workbook:
- GPU families: H100 for latency-sensitive 1–2 token/ms workloads; A100G for cost-optimized throughput for batch-heavy embedding pipelines; L4x for low-cost light-weight routing and embedding for high qps.
- Reserve runway: recommend 60% committed pool for steady-state, 25% reserved for predictable bursts (autoscale within the reserved pool), 15% as a paid burst lane (on-demand) to cover unexpected events.
- Fallback: define a graceful fallback policy that routes to quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) with documented quality delta and an online feature flag per model to pin versions.

I'll attach a short annex on price-band structure once Jordan returns the profile inputs.

—Ben
Account Executive

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Mar 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: RFP: dedicated reservation sizing workbook + stress acceptance criteria

Jordan / Ben / Soojin —

I've sketched the acceptance criteria that Ops teams usually run against our reserved pools. Please review and we can paste into the workbook as the "Stress & Acceptance" tab:

- Load test: 60-minute soak at 1.5x steady-state followed by 20-minute surge at requested burst multiple (we need Elena's burst multiplier).
- Tail SLO: 99.9th token latency must be within agreed SLA (example: <150ms for chat model on H100; <400ms for quantized A100 variant).
- Cold-start recovery: KV-cache warm-up pattern evaluated by measuring token time and throughput over first 3 minutes after a cold restart; cache warm-up should recover to >85% baseline within 4 minutes.
- Bumping & eviction: documented eviction policy for multi-tenant reserved pools and guaranteed preemption window (e.g., 60 seconds).
- Functional: pinned-model test to validate version pinning and deterministic inference for compliance (sample deterministic run of 1000 prompts).

Sooj — can you add a short note on model quantization behavior and quality deltas we can use in the price/quality tradeoff table?

-Kim
Principal Solutions Engineer

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: RFP: dedicated reservation sizing workbook + stress acceptance criteria

Kim / Jordan —

Short quantization note for the workbook:
- H100: best for int8/float16 paths; quantization typically not recommended for highest-accuracy large planning models but viable for assistant models with <2% metric delta on majority of evals.
- A100: supports aggressive 4-bit quant workflows with larger quality delta (~3–6%) on instruction-heavy prompts; great for embeddings and batchified workloads.
- L4: optimized for ONNX and small-quantized pipelines — cost-effective for high-qps low-latency use cases but not suitable as primary reasoning model.

I also recommend we include an explicit quality regression testing step in the runbook (baseline prompts + holdout set) and specify what delta triggers rollbacks.

-Soojin
Applied ML / Inference Optimization

From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <procurement@stratoshealth.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@stratoshealth.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: dedicated reservation sizing workbook + stress acceptance criteria

Elena / Samir —

Thanks for the workbook — attached is our completed runbook and a short narrative describing three sizing scenarios (conservative / balanced / aggressive), the recommended GPU mixes (H100-heavy for latency SLOs, A100 for throughput/embedding lanes, L4 for high-qps light inference), and the stress/acceptance matrix we propose. High-level summary below:

- Conservative: 40% H100, 40% A100, 20% L4. Targets: steady-state throughput to cover 95% of traffic; burst capacity via paid burst lane. Tail SLO target: 99.9th <250ms on chat flows.
- Balanced: 50% H100, 35% A100, 15% L4. Targets: smoother headroom for short bursts (2–5x), improved tail performance.
- Aggressive: 65% H100, 25% A100, 10% L4. Targets: optimized for low-latency product features with higher committed spend.

Stress/acceptance highlights:
- 60min soak at 1.5x then 20min surge at 5x (sample stress we run).
- KV-cache warm-up measured and reported in the acceptance artifact; recovery target >85% within 4 minutes.
- Fallback: automatic routing to pinned quantized variants (if elected) with explicit quality delta documented; an operator-triggered failover to a regional backup if sustained exhaustion beyond 10 minutes.

Attachments: Stratos_RFP_Workbook.xlsx (completed)
Attachment: runway_gpu_mix_v1.pdf (two-page scenario summary)

Next steps: Ben will provide price bands in a separate email later today. Please confirm the expected burst multiplier and average token sizes (in/out) so we can finalize numeric throughput cells in the workbook.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
